# Security and data: build rules

Apply these rules while you build. Domains or criteria whose `applies_if` flags are false in `.quality/project.json` do not apply to this project. Before you call a task done, check your work against the criteria of the domains you touched: each one must be true and verifiable.

If a stack module of the quality pack is installed (qp-nextjs, qp-node-api, qp-vps), its rules skill adds stack-specific rules on top of these.

## Security (SEC)

Secret protection, input validation, permissions, rate limiting and security headers.

Rules:

- No secret in the code, the Git repo or the client bundle; server-side environment variables only.
- Validate every external input server-side with a schema (Zod, Valibot…): body, params, query, headers, webhooks, files.
- Check authorisation on every request, server-side, on the requested resource (not just login).
- Rate-limit login, sign-up, password reset, forms and expensive routes.
- Parameterised database queries or ORM; never string concatenation.
- Headers: CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, frame-ancestors.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] SEC-01: No secret in the repo, Git history or client bundle. Check: gitleaks on history; search for keys in the client build; .env ignored by Git.
- [BLOCKER] SEC-02: Every external input is validated server-side with a schema (only if: has_backend). Check: Read every route, server action, webhook handler and upload.
- [BLOCKER] SEC-03: Authorisation checked server-side on every resource (no IDOR) (only if: has_auth). Check: For each protected route: can a user read or change another user's resource by changing the ID?
- [BLOCKER] SEC-04: No dependency with a known critical or high vulnerability. Check: npm audit, pnpm audit or osv-scanner.
- [major] SEC-05: Rate limiting on sensitive and expensive routes (only if: has_backend). Check: Login, sign-up, password reset, forms, calls to paid APIs.
- [major] SEC-06: Security headers present and CSP without needless unsafe-inline. Check: Request against production or staging; check every header.
- [major] SEC-07: Sessions and passwords handled correctly (only if: has_auth). Check: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite cookies; argon2 or bcrypt hashing; invalidation on logout; CSRF protection.
- [major] SEC-08: No injection: parameterised queries, escaped HTML, no command execution with user input. Check: Search for $queryRaw, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval, exec, child_process with external input.
- [major] SEC-09: Uploads restricted in type and size, stored outside the executable root (only if: has_uploads). Check: Real type check, maximum size, regenerated file name.
- [minor] SEC-10: Errors do not leak internal details. Check: No stack trace, SQL query or server path in production responses.
- [minor] SEC-11: In-depth security audit run at every major release. Check: Dated and tracked report from the security-audit skill (Cloudflare).

## Privacy (PRV)

Collection and handling of personal data (GDPR).

Applies when: Collects personal data (forms, accounts, analytics).

Rules:

- Collect only the data the promise needs; every requested field has a reason.
- Keep an up-to-date list of data, purpose, retention period and processors.
- No non-essential cookie or tracker before consent; refusing as easy as accepting.
- Let users export and delete their data.
- Never write personal data into logs.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] PRV-01: No non-essential tracker set before consent. Check: Load the page without consenting: list cookies, localStorage and third-party requests.
- [major] PRV-02: Accurate and accessible privacy policy. Check: It matches the data actually collected and the processors actually used.
- [major] PRV-03: Minimal collection: no field or tracker without a purpose. Check: Compare forms and data models with the processing register.
- [major] PRV-04: Users can delete and export their data (only if: has_auth). Check: Account deletion that really erases (or anonymises) the linked data.
- [major] PRV-05: No personal data in logs or error tools. Check: Read log calls and Sentry or equivalent config (scrubbing).
- [minor] PRV-06: Retention periods defined and enforced. Check: Purge job or documented rule for inactive accounts, logs, backups.

## Data (DAT)

Data integrity and consistency.

Applies when: Database.

Rules:

- Essential business rules also live in the database: foreign keys, NOT NULL, unique constraints, CHECK.
- Every schema change goes through a versioned migration, reviewed and tested on a copy.
- Operations that change several tables run in a transaction.
- Dates in UTC in the database, amounts as integers (cents) or decimals, never floats.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] DAT-01: Migrations are versioned and the database matches the schema. Check: prisma migrate status (or equivalent) shows no drift; no manual changes in production.
- [major] DAT-02: Integrity constraints in the database (foreign keys, unique, NOT NULL). Check: Read the schema: declared relations, required fields not nullable, business uniqueness.
- [major] DAT-03: Multiple writes inside transactions. Check: Search for related write sequences outside a transaction.
- [major] DAT-04: Amounts and dates stored in safe types. Check: No Float for money; dates in UTC with time zone handled on display.
- [minor] DAT-05: Destructive migrations are reversible or preceded by a backup. Check: Column or table drop: rollback plan or documented backup.
- [minor] DAT-06: Indexes on filtered and joined columns. Check: Compare frequent queries with declared indexes.

## Compliance (LEG)

Applicable legal obligations and licences. This referential is not legal advice.

Rules:

- At /kickoff, identify the country, the publisher type (individual, company) and the resulting obligations; the compliance-fr module details France.
- Check the licence of every dependency, font, image and icon before adding it.
- Credit resources that require it in a dedicated file or in the footer.

Done means:

- [BLOCKER] LEG-01: The publisher's mandatory notices are present. Check: Legal notice or imprint depending on the country (see the country compliance module).
- [major] LEG-02: Dependency licences compatible with the project's use. Check: license-checker or equivalent; no incompatible or missing GPL/AGPL licence.
- [major] LEG-03: Fonts, images, icons and sounds used under a valid licence. Check: Source and licence documented for every third-party asset.
- [major] LEG-04: Terms of use or sale published and accepted (only if: has_accounts_or_sales). Check: Terms accessible; timestamped acceptance at sign-up or purchase.
- [minor] LEG-05: Legal accessibility obligations assessed. Check: Depending on country and activity (e.g. European Accessibility Act for some services): statement if required.
- [minor] LEG-06: Third-party content and trademarks used with permission. Check: Logos, excerpts, content APIs: terms of use respected.
